extracted.intended_audience: NRC licensees, licensee employees, attorneys practicing before the NRC, and NRC officials conducting subpoenas/investigations
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedures governing sequestration of witnesses, exclusion of counsel, and related procedural safeguards during NRC interviews conducted under subpoena (10 CFR part 19 amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Exclusion" means the removal of counsel from interviews whenever the NRC official conducting the interview has a reasonable basis to believe that counsel’s representation of multiple interests will obstruct, impede, or impair the particular investigation, inspection or inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the regulatory definition added in §19.3 and forms the statutory threshold for excluding counsel; it emphasizes multiple representation as the triggering condition and ties exclusion to effect on the investigation (obstruct, impede, impair).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Sequestration
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sequestration" means the separation or isolation of witnesses and their attorneys from other witnesses and their attorneys during an interview conducted as part of an investigation, inspection, or other inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the regulatory definition added in §19.3 and informs the procedural requirement that follows (see §19.18(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequestration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All witnesses compelled by subpoena to submit to agency interviews shall be sequestered unless the official conducting the interviews permits otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affords the interviewing official discretion to waive sequestration, but creates a default rule of isolation to protect interview integrity and witness candor (§19.18(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to counsel subject to exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Any witness compelled by subpoena may be accompanied, represented, and advised by counsel of his or her choice; however, when the agency official determines after consultation with the Office of the General Counsel that a reasonable basis exists to believe the investigation will be obstructed, impeded or impaired by an attorney's representation of multiple interests, the official may prohibit that attorney from being present during the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances the statutory right to counsel (5 U.S.C. 555(b)) with investigative integrity; explicitly requires consultation with OGC prior to exclusion and ties exclusion to a "reasonable basis" standard (§19.18(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for exclusion: reasonable basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion is permitted where there is a "reasonable basis to believe" that counsel’s representation of multiple interests will "obstruct, impede or impair" the investigation or inspection, directly or indirectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule deliberately adopts a less exacting "reasonable basis" standard than the D.C. Circuit's Csapo "concrete evidence" standard, justified by NRC's public health-and-safety responsibilities; the focus is on potential impairment of investigatory process rather than requiring proof that impairment already occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations apply to all persons who receive, possess, use, or transfer material licensed by the NRC under specified parts (including part 50 and part 72) and to interviews of individuals under subpoena in NRC investigations and inspections, other than NRC employees or NRC contractors; the part does not apply to subpoenas issued pursuant to 10 CFR 2.720.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies covered subject matter, licensee population, and explicit exception for certain subpoenas (2.720); use this to determine whether §19 rules govern a given interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances warranting exclusion (substantive examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion contemplated only where counsel's multiple representation poses a threat to NRC's ability to develop credible facts or where the Commission could reasonably expect to obtain necessary safety information only if counsel representing the witness did not also represent other interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: investigations requiring secrecy that cannot be maintained if licensee/others are apprised of inspection specifics; situations where employees must divulge information adverse to employer interests; where witness has expressed desire for confidentiality unknown to counsel. Exclusion is grounded in protecting investigatory confidentiality/public safety rather than in legal-ethics violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with Office of General Counsel (OGC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency official conducting the inquiry must determine exclusion "after consultation with the Office of the General Counsel."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required step to confine exclusion authority within lawful limits and to provide an internal safeguard against arbitrary exclusions; part of the procedural protections accompanying exclusion decisions (§19.18(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written statement of reasons for exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The interviewing official must provide the witness whose counsel has been excluded and the excluded counsel a written statement of the reasons supporting the decision to exclude no later than five working days after the exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule requires explanation in every instance and preservation of reasons in writing to enable judicial or administrative challenge; this was adopted to address commenter concerns about unfettered discretion (§19.18(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to administrative appeal/motion to quash and stay
rubrics_metrics.description: Within five days after receipt of the written notification, a witness whose counsel has been excluded may appeal the exclusion decision by filing a motion to quash the subpoena with the Commission; filing the motion to quash will stay the effectiveness of the subpoena pending the Commission's decision on the motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an expedited administrative remedy (five-day filing deadline) intended to balance prompt investigations with due process; the stay provision preserves the witness's rights while the Commission reviews the exclusion (§19.18(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for conducting the interview after exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where counsel is excluded, at the witness’s request the interview may (1) proceed without counsel, (2) be delayed for a reasonable period to permit retention of new counsel, or (3) be rescheduled to a subsequent date set by the NRC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides flexibility to accommodate witness interests while protecting investigation timeliness; the definition of "reasonable period" is case-by-case (see guidance entry on reasonable period). (§19.18(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable period to retain new counsel: factors for determination
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes a reasonable period of time to retain new counsel must be determined case-by-case taking into account circumstances including the apparent availability of experienced counsel for the particular witness, complexity of the case, need for counsel to familiarize with facts, and the Commission’s need to conclude an investigation or inspection promptly to protect public health and safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble clarifies that illustrative examples (e.g., one week) are not binding; decision-makers must weigh counsel availability, case complexity, and public-safety/expedition imperatives in setting delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural limitations and non-requirement of pre-exclusion fact-finding
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule does not require agency officials to undertake fact-finding proceedings in advance of excluding counsel, nor to make factual findings prior to exclusion; instead, the rule requires consultation with OGC and issuance of written reasons after exclusion and affords an administrative appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission rejected commenters' requests for pre-exclusion adjudicatory proceedings, concluding that the combination of OGC consultation, written reasons, and right to challenge provides sufficient safeguards against arbitrary exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale: public-safety justification for less exacting standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC concluded that because NRC investigations implicate immediate public health and safety concerns, the "concrete evidence" standard of Csapo (SEC context) would be inappropriate and a less exacting "reasonable basis" standard is justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains policy basis for the chosen standard and helps interpreters distinguish NRC practice from other agencies (e.g., SEC) where different stakes might dictate a stricter standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion is not an ethics-based disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion decisions under the rule are not based on legal-ethics considerations; ethical considerations are essentially immaterial to the decision to exclude, which is based on the need to maintain confidentiality and protect the investigation's integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the rule's exclusion authority is a protective investigatory measure (not a determination of an attorney's ethical fitness) and cites Csapo in support of this framing.
